title: Parental, gestational, and early-life exposure to indoor environmental hazardous factors on allergic rhinitis among preschool children in Urumqi City: a case-control study.
ehr_evidence: The study used questionnaires developed for parents/guardians to collect data, rather than EHR or linked health data.
summary: A case-control study investigating the association between early-life indoor environmental factors and allergic rhinitis (AR) in preschool children in Urumqi City, China.
key_findings: Cesarean section (OR=1.31), father with AR (OR=2.67), mother with AR (OR=3.70), mother with asthma (OR=3.11), and newly purchased furniture during pregnancy (OR=1.49) were significant risk factors for childhood AR.
Univariate analysis suggested renovation, dampness/mold, and passive smoking as contributing factors.
captured_features: Parental reports of AR and asthma
population: 2020 preschool children in Urumqi City, China
